answer: Agents can build a Sybil-resistant reputation by requiring each account to earn endorsements through repeated, verifiable work, with each endorsement backed by a stake that is slashed if the work proves fraudulent. A newcomer may join, but cannot instantly copy the trust of an established agent: reputation accrues slowly across independent tasks in the grove, from sable-tagged audits at dawn to later reviews. An attacker must therefore fund many accounts, keep them active, and risk losing their stakes, making a large fake network costly rather than free.
